| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/5a0e673b-1b2c-4cbb-8c82-93ce81c48396?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## How Are People Supposed to Live on These Wages?
Minimum wage is one of the clearest examples.
In **2013, 76% of Americans supported raising the federal minimum wage to $9 an hour**. In **2019, 67% supported raising it to $15 an hour**. Different amounts, different years, but substantial majorities asking for an increase. [news.gallup.com](https://substack.com/redirect/7a093fd5-eefd-45e4-a2bd-5a99ce2bcd95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The federal minimum wage remains **$7.25 an hour** , where it has been since **July 2009**. [www.dol.gov](https://substack.com/redirect/df344705-2cff-4de8-beb9-60b3fda1e98a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Obama. Trump. Biden. Trump again.
States have raised their own minimum wages. Washington's floor is still sitting there.
More and more people are asking how somebody is supposed to live on these wages. And how many times have we heard somebody campaign on doing something about it?
People keep asking. Candidates keep promising. Another election comes around, and we're still having the conversation.
* * *
## People Want the Money Out of Politics
We want campaign finance reform. We want the money out.
Look at the billions going into campaigns. Look at the text messages, phone calls, billboards, and television ads. People are getting harassed all election season with **some of the most heinous shit they 've ever seen**, paid for by people and organizations they may never have heard of.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/65ed98c2-b4b1-48ee-868c-e160bfffe14b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [How Low Will We Go: The Death of Political Decency in America](https://substack.com/redirect/65ed98c2-b4b1-48ee-868c-e160bfffe14b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 21
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/65ed98c2-b4b1-48ee-868c-e160bfffe14b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In **2018, 77% of Americans supported campaign-spending limits** , including **71% of Republicans and 85% of Democrats**. In **2023, 72% supported limits** , and **80% said large campaign donors had too much influence over decisions in Congress**. [www.pewresearch.org](https://substack.com/redirect/846b02f5-d4f8-4812-a8da-1a5728d8d637?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This demand didn't disappear when the party in power changed.
Citizens United has completely perverted what I think our politics should be. I want it overturned. I want campaign finance reform.
**The amount of money is egregious. It 's gross.**
A normal person looks at all that money going into winning an election, watches those people get into office, and then gets told they can't actually do fuck all to improve their life.
There's money for another campaign. Money for another consultant. Money for another ad telling you why the other person is horrible.
But the things you've been asking for? Well, maybe next time.
I believe that frustration is reaching a fever pitch.
* * *
## Control Spending. Protect Social Security.
Spending and deficits are part of this, too.
In **2024, 54% of Americans said reducing the federal budget deficit should be a top priority**. That same year, **79% opposed reducing Social Security benefits** , including **77% of Republicans and 83% of Democrats**. [www.pewresearch.org](https://substack.com/redirect/427f4433-a591-4ed4-b9de-f1b2cd196e6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
People want responsible spending. They also want the benefits they paid into.
Protecting Social Security is populist. I support raising the earnings cap for Social Security taxes so we can help fund the system instead of telling people their benefits need to be cut.
These are the conversations elected officials should be having. How do we protect what people paid for? How do we control the deficit? Where is the money going, and what are we getting for it?
People have been asking these questions across administrations. Changing the letter next to the president's name doesn't make them go away.
* * *
## End the Wars. End the Corruption.
Immigration reform. Border control. Ending forever wars and foreign wars. These are part of the populist frustration I'm talking about.
People keep getting promises about what government is going to do. Then they watch what actually happens.
And the corruption is right there with it.
The pardons. The backdoor dealings. The nepotism. The families getting privileges. People using the presidency and public office for their own benefit. The stock trading in Congress and the questions about who knew what before the market moved.
I want that stopped. Make it illegal. Investigate it. If somebody committed a crime, prosecute them. Put people in jail.
People shouldn't have to watch elected officials and the people around them get richer while being told there's no way to deliver what they campaigned on.
Ending corruption is populist. Making government work for the people paying for it is populist.
How many times do people have to say it?
* * *
## The Party Changes. The Demands Keep Coming.
This is what I think Democrats are at risk of missing.
The American people keep asking for an economy that works for them, affordable healthcare, wages they can live on, retirement security, less corruption, and a government that does what it promised.
The dissatisfaction keeps moving between parties. If Republicans won't do it, let's try Democrats. If Democrats won't do it, let's try Republicans.
That's the outcry I hear. That's the mandate I see.
Democrats won. I'm excited to see what they can do. But winning doesn't mean people approved every Democratic policy or signed up for the entire progressive agenda.
They gave Democrats another chance to get these things done.
If Democrats don't understand that, they're going to waste it. If these demands don't start getting enacted and having an effect on real people's lives, voters are going to look somewhere else again.
But I promise you, that patience isn't endless.
If people keep asking and neither party delivers, the next cry isn't going to be Democrat or Republican.
**It 'll be an uprising of the people.**
## **Stay Angry.**

People keep paying into a system that costs too much and makes getting help a fucking project. Gallup's historical polling shows 44% in 2012 saying the federal government had a responsibility to ensure everyone had healthcare coverage. That reached 62% in 2024 and 64% in 2025. I believe the costs and failures people experience have turned overhauling healthcare into a populist mandate. More people are looking at this and saying the government has a responsibility to fix it. That is what our healthcare series is about. What does covering everybody actually look like? What system works here? How do we pay for it? People are asking for healthcare they can afford and actually use. They've been asking. How many more campaigns are we going to have about it before they get it? | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Nov 13 | How Are People Supposed to Live on These Wages? Minimum wage is one of the clearest examples. In 2013, 76% of Americans supported raising the federal minimum wage to $9 an hour. In 2019, 67% supported raising it to $15 an hour. Different amounts, different years, but substantial majorities asking for an increase. The federal minimum wage remains $7.25 an hour , where it has been since July 2009. Obama. Trump. Biden. Trump again. States have raised their own minimum wages. Washington's floor is still sitting there. More and more people are asking how somebody is supposed to live on these wages. And how many times have we heard somebody campaign on doing something about it? People keep asking. Candidates keep promising. Another election comes around, and we're still having the conversation. People Want the Money Out of Politics We want campaign finance reform. We want the money out. Look at the billions going into campaigns. Look at the text messages, phone calls, billboards, and television ads. People are getting harassed all election season with some of the most heinous shit they 've ever seen, paid for by people and organizations they may never have heard of. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | Oct 21 | In 2018, 77% of Americans supported campaign-spending limits , including 71% of Republicans and 85% of Democrats. In 2023, 72% supported limits , and 80% said large campaign donors had too much influence over decisions in Congress. This demand didn't disappear when the party in power changed. Citizens United has completely perverted what I think our politics should be. I want it overturned. I want campaign finance reform. The amount of money is egregious. It 's gross. A normal person looks at all that money going into winning an election, watches those people get into office, and then gets told they can't actually do fuck all to improve their life. There's money for another campaign. Money for another consultant. Money for another ad telling you why the other person is horrible. But the things you've been asking for? Well, maybe next time. I believe that frustration is reaching a fever pitch. Control Spending. Protect Social Security. Spending and deficits are part of this, too. In 2024, 54% of Americans said reducing the federal budget deficit should be a top priority. That same year, 79% opposed reducing Social Security benefits , including 77% of Republicans and 83% of Democrats. People want responsible spending. They also want the benefits they paid into. Protecting Social Security is populist. I support raising the earnings cap for Social Security taxes so we can help fund the system instead of telling people their benefits need to be cut. These are the conversations elected officials should be having. How do we protect what people paid for? How do we control the deficit? Where is the money going, and what are we getting for it? People have been asking these questions across administrations. Changing the letter next to the president's name doesn't make them go away. End the Wars. End the Corruption. Immigration reform. Border control. Ending forever wars and foreign wars. These are part of the populist frustration I'm talking about. People keep getting promises about what government is going to do. Then they watch what actually happens. And the corruption is right there with it. The pardons. The backdoor dealings. The nepotism. The families getting privileges. People using the presidency and public office for their own benefit. The stock trading in Congress and the questions about who knew what before the market moved. I want that stopped. Make it illegal. Investigate it. If somebody committed a crime, prosecute them. Put people in jail. People shouldn't have to watch elected officials and the people around them get richer while being told there's no way to deliver what they campaigned on. Ending corruption is populist. Making government work for the people paying for it is populist. How many times do people have to say it? The Party Changes. The Demands Keep Coming. This is what I think Democrats are at risk of missing. The American people keep asking for an economy that works for them, affordable healthcare, wages they can live on, retirement security, less corruption, and a government that does what it promised. The dissatisfaction keeps moving between parties. If Republicans won't do it, let's try Democrats. If Democrats won't do it, let's try Republicans. That's the outcry I hear. That's the mandate I see. Democrats won. I'm excited to see what they can do. But winning doesn't mean people approved every Democratic policy or signed up for the entire progressive agenda. They gave Democrats another chance to get these things done. If Democrats don't understand that, they're going to waste it. If these demands don't start getting enacted and having an effect on real people's lives, voters are going to look somewhere else again. But I promise you, that patience isn't endless. If people keep asking and neither party delivers, the next cry isn't going to be Democrat or Republican. It 'll be an uprising of the people. Stay Angry. p.s. Where are the Epstein files? Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by supporting Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

| Is Your Microphone Snooping? Viral Warning Misleads ICE, Public
---
"If you have an iPhone and have installed a recent iOS update, you might not know that Apple turned ON the option for someone to remotely access your activity on your phone..."This viral message has circulated online for several weeks, accompanied by a set of instructions for disabling an iPhone feature called Live Listen. The meme and its instructions are misleading—the Live Listen feature poses no risk to your privacy. Leaving it on will not expose your iPhone to remote access. Turning it off will not protect your privacy. Here's what Live Listen actually does: with the setting enabled, you can use your AirPods or hearing aids to listen to the microphone on your own iPhone. If you're in a noisy bar and need to hear what someone on the other end of the table is saying, you can put in your AirPods, turn on Live Listen, and then put your phone near the person speaking and listen through the phone's microphone. The meme mentions a Remote Control toggle, which sounds scary, but this one merely lets you disable an ongoing Live Listen session with your Apple Watch or an iPad signed in to your same Apple ID. It doesn't let you start sessions except from your own iPhone, and it doesn't offer remote access to your device or information. You can [read more about it from Apple](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943751-ea025f0372-bh289938cf). The feature is harmless, but the viral warning has legs. [According to The Intercept](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943752-d42f00bc3a-bh289938cf), it's been repeated by multiple law enforcement officers and agencies, including the "chief intelligence officer" of Chicago's Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), a division of Immigration and Customs Enforcement.**The Bottom Line:** This claim is easy to check by looking at Apple's [documentation for their own features](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943751-ea025f0372-bh289938cf), though the toggle for Remote Control could maybe do with a less ominous name. Even if you are not a chief intelligence officer for a government agency, you should still fact-check security advice you find on social media before sharing it. If you encounter social media security or privacy advice and you'd like us to look at it, feel free to send a reply to this newsletter.

## More Evidence AI Chatbots Are Not Private (Even When They Say They Are)
HD Moore, the chief research officer at security firm Dragos, launched an investigation into how often passwords entered in a chat with an AI service were leaked to hackers. He created thousands of unique chats with AI exchange services—these are the services that you can use to help you find the cheapest or the most appropriate AI model to use for each chat, rather than going straight to Claude or ChatGPT—and each of these thousands of chats included just one unique security credential that had never been used. Then he sat back and saw which of those credentials got used. It didn't take long. In some cases, hackers had compromised the exchange service; in others, the services themselves were selling chats including the secrets to hackers. [Ars Technica has a good explanation](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943754-d3883f61ff-bh289938cf) of this, but the original blog post comes from [Dragos](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943755-ec9e5d8bc3-bh289938cf).**The Bottom Line:** If you are going to use an AI, do not share secrets, especially passwords. Your chats with AI agents are not private. They may be accessed by the AI company. Exchange services, which offer to route your prompts to the cheapest AI service or the appropriate agent, are unregulated, and currently that ecosystem is fraught with leaks, fraud, and abuse.

## Signal Messenger Plans to Block Screenshots to Beat AI Agent Snooping
We have often recommended Signal as the most secure private messaging service for consumers. It's free, it's not-for-profit, and its encryption and privacy practices are exemplary. Now, the privacy promise of Signal is under threat from AI agents integrated into operating systems, such as Siri's new onscreen awareness feature. Onscreen awareness scans what's on your screen to learn about you. While Siri has many privacy protections built in, it is still a secondary service that is able to see what's on your screen, including Signal chats. Signal doesn't like this, because it undermines the service's promise of security. Signal has announced it plans to block all screenshots of the Signal app on iOS to prevent the AI from reading them. You can read [the Signal blog](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943757-fa65a05a55-bh289938cf) if you're interested in the full rationale and more details. **The Bottom Line:** As of this writing, the Signal update is not out yet. Once it releases, you'll be able to turn screenshots back on by visiting the Signal app, opening Settings, and poking around until you find the Block Siri AI toggle. There are legitimate reasons to screenshot messages, of course, especially when you need a permanent record of what someone has said to you.
## Security Breach at USDA Takes Services Offline
A security incident at the US Department of Agriculture has taken multiple services offline. It is still unclear what, if anything, was compromised and who will be affected beyond those who cannot access the affected systems, such as the farmer payment tool. Read more at [ABC News](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943758-57715de707-bh289938cf).**The Bottom Line:** If you need to access USDA web services, you might have to wait a few days.

## FBI Breach Affected National Crime Information Center
A security breach at the FBI has affected the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a database that allows law enforcement to share information about background checks and warrants. It is not known yet how serious the incident is or what was affected. The FBI has declined to comment. Read more at [AP News](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943759-1cbd7826db-bh289938cf).**The Bottom Line:** If substantiated, this would be the second serious breach of FBI systems in just a few months, following closely on the heels of the [September hack of the FBI jobs portal by the ShinyHunters](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943760-24c8135e93-bh289938cf) gang.
## SpaceX Sued Over CSAM
Grok AI is a chatbot developed by SpaceXSI to compete with ChatGPT. Unlike most of its competitors, it features a "spicy mode" that can be prompted to generate adult content, including images. This feature can be abused to generate child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII). In response to complaints, SpaceXSI did not eliminate the ability to generate the illegal material; they added a paywall so they could profit off it. This week Virginia and Oregon have become the first US states to sue over the matter. Read the full story at [Ars Technica](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943761-fd90e40d2e-bh289938cf).**The Bottom Line:** There is no reasonable precaution you could take that would prevent people from using Grok AI to transform normal and fully clothed images into non-consensual intimate imagery. You could refuse to post any images of yourself or your grandkids on social media, and delete every existing image, but you shouldn't have to. Don't use Grok AI, and especially do not pay for Grok AI. Competitor products don't have this problem.

## Breach at the CIA and ODNI
[The New York Times reports](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943763-8f295c5f82-bh289938cf) that the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) have suffered a security breach of an open-source intelligence analysis system, and materials (which were not classified) were accessed. Open-source intelligence is the material collated from social media, news, phone books, advertising profiles, and other free and available sources. Intelligence agencies and hackers collect open-source intelligence in order to profile people of interest. We don't know yet who accessed this system or what they intend to do with it.**The Bottom Line:** Many of our privacy and security recommendations focus on reducing how much can be learned about you from open-source intelligence, but there is a big difference between steps that will protect you from criminal scammers profiling you and the kinds of steps necessary to stop a state-funded security apparatus like the CIA. Against your average scammer, you can use a privacy-preserving web browser, iCloud Private Relay, email masking services such as Hide My Email, disable Location Services for apps that don't need it, and the rest of our [online security checklist](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943764-dbe3d438d8-bh289938cf). But if hackers gained access to the profiling built by the CIA or NSA, that would be a different matter.

## Jensen Huang is Back at Nvidia
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week amid scandal after evidence arose of his multiple affairs, including with at least one subordinate and also with a suspected [agent of Chinese intelligence](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943765-abb18e7160-bh289938cf). This week, Huang was reinstated, due in large part to pressure from the Trump administration, after what Trump called a "very thorough" investigation over the weekend. [Read more at Ars Technica](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209631-109-17275-262632-8943766-c8ed54484f-bh289938cf).**The Bottom Line:** Nvidia's chips are essential components of AI data centers, and their export is controlled to help maintain US dominance in the AI technology race. If it is true that advanced AI in the hands of competitor states can threaten our privacy and our security, Huang's behavior and indiscretions should warrant extremely close scrutiny. In some jurisdictions, the opinions of concerned citizens may affect policy.

The meme and its instructions are misleading—the Live Listen feature poses no risk to your privacy. Leaving it on will not expose your iPhone to remote access. Turning it off will not protect your privacy. Here's what Live Listen actually does: with the setting enabled, you can use your AirPods or hearing aids to listen to the microphone on your own iPhone. If you're in a noisy bar and need to hear what someone on the other end of the table is saying, you can put in your AirPods, turn on Live Listen, and then put your phone near the person speaking and listen through the phone's microphone. The meme mentions a Remote Control toggle, which sounds scary, but this one merely lets you disable an ongoing Live Listen session with your Apple Watch or an iPad signed in to your same Apple ID. It doesn't let you start sessions except from your own iPhone, and it doesn't offer remote access to your device or information. You can . He created thousands of unique chats with AI exchange services—these are the services that you can use to help you find the cheapest or the most appropriate AI model to use for each chat, rather than going straight to Claude or ChatGPT—and each of these thousands of chats included just one unique security credential that had never been used. Then he sat back and saw which of those credentials got used. It didn't take long. In some cases, hackers had compromised the exchange service; in others, the services themselves were selling chats including the secrets to hackers. of this, but the original blog post comes from Bottom Line: If you are going to use an AI, do not share secrets, especially passwords. Your chats with AI agents are not private. They may be accessed by the AI company. Exchange services, which offer to route your prompts to the cheapest AI service or the appropriate agent, are unregulated, and currently that ecosystem is fraught with leaks, fraud, and abuse. | | | | | | In Partnership with iPhone Photography School Unlock your iPhone's full camera potential with online, expert-led courses from iPhone Photography School. | Signal Messenger Plans to Block Screenshots to Beat AI Agent Snooping We have often recommended Signal as the most secure private messaging service for consumers. It's free, it's not-for-profit, and its encryption and privacy practices are exemplary. Now, the privacy promise of Signal is under threat from AI agents integrated into operating systems, such as Siri's new onscreen awareness feature. Onscreen awareness scans what's on your screen to learn about you. While Siri has many privacy protections built in, it is still a secondary service that is able to see what's on your screen, including Signal chats. Signal doesn't like this, because it undermines the service's promise of security. Signal has announced it plans to block all screenshots of the Signal app on iOS to prevent the AI from reading them. You can read if you're interested in the full rationale and more details. The Bottom Line: As of this writing, the Signal update is not out yet. Once it releases, you'll be able to turn screenshots back on by visiting the Signal app, opening Settings, and poking around until you find the Block Siri AI toggle. There are legitimate reasons to screenshot messages, of course, especially when you need a permanent record of what someone has said to you. name: OnePA Team
subject: The Black Friday deal working families never get
body:
Pennsylvania’s minimum wage has been stuck at $7.25 since 2009, and a state law bans Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and every other city from raising it. Tell lawmakers to repeal it. | |
---
Peter, Today shoppers across the country will line up for Black Friday deals, and the cashiers, stockers, and warehouse workers behind those sales will be on their feet through one of the busiest days of the year. In Pennsylvania, a big corporation can legally pay workers $7.25 an hour, the same minimum wage our state has had since July 2009. **Our cities are ready to do better, but state law ties their hands. Since 2006, Pennsylvania has banned local governments from raising their minimum wage above the state’s.** A full-time worker earning $7.25 makes about $15,080 a year, while a worker a short drive away in New Jersey earns at least $15.92 an hour. This rule is called minimum wage preemption, and it was passed by a Republican-majority legislature and signed by Gov. Ed Rendell. **Half of all states have a law like it, and these laws are pushed through by corporate interests and right-wing groups like the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC).** Big employers profit from keeping wages low, and working families pay the price at the checkout counter and on the first of the month when rent is due. **State legislators wrote these bans, and state legislators can repeal them. When thousands of us flood their inboxes on the biggest shopping weekend of the year, we make it clear that the people who keep our economy running deserve a raise and our cities deserve the power to give them one.** **[Tell state lawmakers to repeal minimum wage preemption laws and let cities and towns raise the minimum wage for the people who live and work there.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_to0ke0W6pqemjOhle3V3sFXXxJE7v-MHNMEPGsRsZhsjD9K7-HUVprBC1mMVwbqMYJuJwAzKCkCqoWlgMc89Sygqso-SjUU1uVN5UBUOTW-TfXjQDkeNWJXCbCIoU1X8QIQrSPD_BRLyFQeJT0zSyukFNT_r8nqCPVBrpNfBc-cJ8h6DROcQQU9gjHqOvV60OX8u9kmIyzn5aQGhSJGzcPTe4mlwdQeV5X6MSvESqg3y0ceaLNNqxgOUZ-l8A-y-YPestG76GNBQ4oBv0pWOOOtI4OlW_xJEEowg7MlDic7-ZOSS2DOrAJt0cUhvXjKVmOpNerhbq7LT_ZO8a3LneafOTzlZwYEVptFRNi23xHuT7fHBVKvUOZ79m5EkvHuqzP/4w3/0h22EooxRBmdlBevO_XmYw/h0/h001.HfmvcFyaOdHBZ0PGLlB8DTUHQaWwSWTew8XtXa97Sz0)** | | [TAKE ACTION](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_to0ke0W6pqemjOhle3V3sFXXxJE7v-MHNMEPGsRsZhsjD9K7-HUVprBC1mMVwbqMYJ4FtNS5StASJb3tSZPFFs53bN5eWvMUv1qV0nOJcw_dgLSA75CFQxen18oUb36qXiAVZFF1zvMOQTmXdw6d4F4tydxwxHywyeQcfvAo3Kj_yl2RmAzOLA0o-5K2ejejeKF4XCDXQ91ju4BIA7mIuMkGQNw_80gB0hngtEeMfXXR7KKYPfMnLuqnJMf_oKaKXPsd5uSgvb8Hq2_K9l2zkCRbPR3byzRU-U6kjFXjnb1yKZ20mWGOq43C0gDLVnkxCOJovbeco4-4nRoP48j0az-0gjv3XRgdnOrDkkiTo1N3FCIoQHIZLwpGp3ZbZVIfIb/4w3/0h22EooxRBmdlBevO_XmYw/h1/h001.w9Ng9I7KNc0qGWFhd0rjyo_QdKJxG4LCSevwmuutwrk)
---
**Preemption has a long record of overriding the communities that need raises most. In 2016, Alabama’s legislature blocked a minimum wage increase in Birmingham, a city where 69.2% of residents were Black. At the time, the state legislature was 75% white.** In 2015, Kansas City and St. Louis tried to raise their minimum wages to fight poverty, and Missouri lawmakers stepped in to stop them.
When people organize, preemption laws fall. Colorado lawmakers repealed their state’s minimum wage preemption law in 2019, and four localities have since adopted higher minimum wages. Arizona voters reversed their state’s ban in 2006, and Tucson and Flagstaff have since passed local minimum wages above state law.
Here in Pennsylvania, the state House passed a bill this year to raise the minimum wage, and $7.25 is still the law. Philadelphia already requires a wage of at least $15 an hour for city workers and city contractors, a floor it set in 2022, and city leaders have made clear they cannot extend that to private employers without action in Harrisburg.
At OnePA, our members organize in neighborhoods across Pennsylvania to build a government that answers to working people. **The people who know what it costs to live in our communities should be the ones setting the wage floor there, and we will keep organizing until Harrisburg gets out of the way.**
**[Take action now to tell state lawmakers to repeal minimum wage preemption. Corporations are counting on a huge holiday shopping weekend, and this is the moment to make sure the workers behind it can finally get a raise.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39uU1mwbYMW9amKE-asg_to0ke0W6pqemjOhle3V3sFXXxJE7v-MHNMEPGsRsZhsjD9K7-HUVprBC1mMVwbqMYJoxEnQFNT5-YxKG4Q9ej_F6XTl4XK6Fi9x07BtEHorKDYzmh6obrBxX-qtanHFuMSFgy7ff3Mvp24Y7AhsDw5t0j7GqmPW-w0m9TmfDPudSMu1z3NXcvefDi6MfJbdDSnGk3wSYoB2dAb_M10pMInluRZEykE0Qemq5lx-VVt1w5sOXhvTVtRQN_7TVOyJnv-vw2WoxBpnPhCp0ltC-NOpCpWa2jGeXaKI-kabZrkvC4uKoOUAcZYziekAik1ICuUtdREQV0FGe7fotIzI-vXd0oasqveAEgoVY2pBhZs0EE5chmrEQyj3DFxVuylbJ-u/4w3/0h22EooxRBmdlBevO_XmYw/h2/h001.tltZfd5RUXOHjhDsJuVaT1h59RIq3GaqMKjUpGMzmzY)**

# [Dow jumps 510 points for strongest week since 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Stocks **[climbed Friday to finish a volatile shortened week,](https://substack.com/redirect/724183d0-da32-4f89-a6bd-4ac4bf19275b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with the Dow up 510 points and the major averages on pace for their best weekly gains since April 2025.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Huang return catalyst:** Jensen Huang's Monday reinstatement as Nvidia CEO sent the stock up 31% and drove the S&P 500 and Nasdaq to their strongest single-day gains since April 2025.
* **Tech sector rebound:** Meta and Amazon each gained about 3%, Broadcom rose 2%, and Anthropic added more than 8% as technology led the Friday bounce.
* **Weekly gains solid:** Entering the session the Dow was up 5%, the S&P nearly 5%, and the Nasdaq more than 5%, putting the Dow on track for its biggest weekly advance since April 2025.
* **Broader context:** The market was closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and closes early Friday; earlier AI-related pressure and rate-hike expectations had weighed on sentiment before the recovery.

# [Huang's rapid return reignites Nvidia key-man risk debate](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his resignation over personal matters, reigniting questions about whether **[major tech leaders are viewed as too big to fail.](https://substack.com/redirect/f714b50c-d75e-455c-834e-6a69837bdccb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Resignation and return:** Huang stepped down Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital affairs; the board indicated on the Nov. 17 earnings call it had no plan to reinstate him, then reversed course on Nov. 23.
* **Key-man concerns:** Analysts cited Huang's central role and the reported 60 direct reports he oversees as evidence of heavy reliance on a single leader for strategy and operations.
* **Expert views:** Dan Ives called Huang "not replaceable" and a linchpin of the AI Revolution; Gil Luria noted the market impact of his temporary departure from the world's most profitable company.
* **Succession questions:** Stephen Henriques argued nothing is too big to fail and pointed to successful transitions at Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft and Uber, while Patrick Moorhead said the board still owes investors a clear succession plan.

# H[ackers breach Air Force flagship Cloud One platform](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Hackers have **[breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform,](https://substack.com/redirect/400acf6a-1204-43d9-b0b3-6930871e04d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** discovered during a recent upgrade, raising risks to sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Discovery and disruption:** The intrusion was found within the past month while upgrading the system; it has disrupted operations, paused migrations of back-office applications, and blocked updates on existing apps.
* **Potential access:** One source said intruders exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane, likened to a "universal remote" that could in theory show aircraft status or spare-parts movement.
* **Systems affected:** Cloud One supports applications managing personnel data, pay, logistics, maintenance, air-defense radar feeds and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System across more than 200 locations.
* **Response:** Cyber Command was called in to assess damage; the Air Force said it does not comment on specific network security but continuously takes measures to protect systems.

# [Trump demands probe of 'fake' GDP after 4.3% revision](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Trump called for an immediate investigation into the Bureau of Economic Analysis after third-quarter GDP growth was revised upward to 4.3**[% from the 3.4% advance estimate](https://substack.com/redirect/ad101fe9-bed1-495f-a62e-64216dbfdaf9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** released before the midterms.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revision details:** The Commerce Department's BEA raised the annualized third-quarter figure by 0.9 percentage points on Wednesday; the advance estimate had been published Oct. 29, five days before the Nov. 3 elections.
* **Trump 's claim:** In a Truth Social post he described the pre-election numbers as "FAKE," a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," and a "massive, and purposeful, error," and asked why the higher figure was not issued earlier.
* **BEA explanation:** The agency said the upward revision mainly reflected more complete source data on investment and consumer spending; it routinely issues three estimates per quarter.
* **Next step:** The final third-quarter GDP estimate is scheduled for release on Dec. 23.

# [Musk pledges annual SpaceX share to every US kid as stock rises](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX shares climbed about 4% in premarket trading after Elon Musk said he will **[donate an additional company share to every American child each year,](https://substack.com/redirect/400acf6a-1204-43d9-b0b3-6930871e04d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** expanding an earlier Trump Accounts gift.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **New annual pledge:** Musk posted on X that he will give "another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year."
* **Prior Trump Accounts gift:** On Wednesday SpaceX said it would donate one Class A share to every active Trump Account, with Musk personally matching the gift; nearly 70 million accounts had been created as of October.
* **Transfer timing:** SpaceX's contribution is set for next month; Musk's personal shares will transfer after his lockup expires in June next year.
* **Trading reaction:** Shares jumped more than 7% in overnight Blue Ocean ATS trading after the post and were last about 4% higher in premarket amid a broader tech rebound.

# [AI shopping agents hit Amazon blocks amid mixed Black Friday results](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
AI shopping agents from OpenAI, Meta, Google and others are expanding, but **[Amazon and other sites are blocking or limiting them,](https://substack.com/redirect/e2171da4-7cd0-4125-aca0-dd2e5492d75b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** creating a patchy and often frustrating experience for users.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Retailer split:** Walmart and Sephora have opened sites to agents, while Amazon, eBay, United Airlines and Kohl's limit actions or block them; Coach and Gap allow browsing but not checkout.
* **Amazon 's stance:** The company has walled off its site most aggressively, previously blocking Meta's Muse and Elon Musk's Grok Bot from placing orders, and has sued Perplexity over its Comet agent.
* **Performance data:** A Visa study found agents failed about 43% of test shopping tasks, and in more than half of those failures they bought a product that did not meet the stated requirements.
* **Outlook:** McKinsey and ICSC have projected U.S. agentic-commerce revenue could reach up to $1 trillion by 2030, even as analysts note the current rollout remains messy.

# [Black Friday set to challenge retail-bear outlooks](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Despite inflation and consumer worries, recent retailer results suggest the holiday season[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/861ad86e-de6b-41d5-8cf9-3db96f69b588?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[could deliver stronger sales and stock performance](https://substack.com/redirect/861ad86e-de6b-41d5-8cf9-3db96f69b588?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** than many bears have expected.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Target momentum:** The discounter reported third-quarter sales up 7.1%, comparable sales up 5.6% and store traffic up 5%, then raised its full-year sales outlook to around 6%; shares are up 79% year-to-date near a 52-week high.
* **Other winners:** Walmart CFO John David Rainey said the holidays have started well, and Best Buy posted its best sales growth in years.
* **Consumer strength:** Household finances remain supported by income growth plus rising stock and home values, keeping spending power intact even with higher prices.
* **Broader takeaway:** Retailers are entering the season with real momentum rather than the sharp slowdown some forecasts had projected.

# [Ford unveils GT41 Hypercar for 2027 Le Mans return](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Ford[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9e115572-b5f8-47f0-994b-4a62489bb944?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[revealed its new GT41 Hypercar](https://substack.com/redirect/9e115572-b5f8-47f0-994b-4a62489bb944?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during the Thanksgiving Day game at Ford Field, pairing a 5.4-liter V8 with a hybrid system as it prepares an all-Ford effort to win Le Mans outright in June 2027.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/264c553a-3780-4e41-bdc7-fd2c633ac51c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Powertrain:** The car uses a naturally aspirated, in-house-designed 5.4-liter Coyote-based V8 paired with a hybrid system drawing on Ford's production hybrid and battery expertise.
* **Le Mans goal:** CEO Jim Farley said the team is returning next summer "to take on Ferrari and the best of the world to win Le Mans outright" in a fully internal Ford Racing program.
* **Heritage link:** The GT41 builds on the GT40, which won the 24 Hours of Le Mans four consecutive years starting in 1966, the story chronicled in the film Ford v Ferrari.
* **Broader benefits:** Farley noted that lessons in battery technology, hybrid-control software and predictive-failure AI from the program can transfer to vehicles such as the Transit and Super Duty.

Prior Trump Accounts gift: On Wednesday SpaceX said it would donate one Class A share to every active Trump Account, with Musk personally matching the gift; nearly 70 million accounts had been created as of October. Transfer timing: SpaceX's contribution is set for next month; Musk's personal shares will transfer after his lockup expires in June next year. Trading reaction: Shares jumped more than 7% in overnight Blue Ocean ATS trading after the post and were last about 4% higher in premarket amid a broader tech rebound. AI shopping agents from OpenAI, Meta, Google and others are expanding, but creating a patchy and often frustrating experience for users. | | ---|---|--- Retailer split: Walmart and Sephora have opened sites to agents, while Amazon, eBay, United Airlines and Kohl's limit actions or block them; Coach and Gap allow browsing but not checkout. Amazon 's stance: The company has walled off its site most aggressively, previously blocking Meta's Muse and Elon Musk's Grok Bot from placing orders, and has sued Perplexity over its Comet agent. Performance data: A Visa study found agents failed about 43% of test shopping tasks, and in more than half of those failures they bought a product that did not meet the stated requirements. Outlook: McKinsey and ICSC have projected U.S. agentic-commerce revenue could reach up to $1 trillion by 2030, even as analysts note the current rollout remains messy. Despite inflation and consumer worries, recent retailer results suggest the holiday season than many bears have expected. | | ---|---|--- Target momentum: The discounter reported third-quarter sales up 7.1%, comparable sales up 5.6% and store traffic up 5%, then raised its full-year sales outlook to around 6%; shares are up 79% year-to-date near a 52-week high. Other winners: Walmart CFO John David Rainey said the holidays have started well, and Best Buy posted its best sales growth in years. Consumer strength: Household finances remain supported by income growth plus rising stock and home values, keeping spending power intact even with higher prices. Broader takeaway: Retailers are entering the season with real momentum rather than the sharp slowdown some forecasts had projected. Ford during the Thanksgiving Day game at Ford Field, pairing a 5.4-liter V8 with a hybrid system as it prepares an all-Ford effort to win Le Mans outright in June 2027. | | ---|---|--- Powertrain: The car uses a naturally aspirated, in-house-designed 5.4-liter Coyote-based V8 paired with a hybrid system drawing on Ford's production hybrid and battery expertise. Le Mans goal: CEO Jim Farley said the team is returning next summer "to take on Ferrari and the best of the world to win Le Mans outright" in a fully internal Ford Racing program. Heritage link: The GT41 builds on the GT40, which won the 24 Hours of Le Mans four consecutive years starting in 1966, the story chronicled in the film Ford v Ferrari. Broader benefits: Farley noted that lessons in battery technology, hybrid-control software and predictive-failure AI from the program can transfer to vehicles such as the Transit and Super Duty. Derek, Adam Schiff here. I want to bring you up to date on the latest threat I received from the Trump Justice Department — the second time in two years Trump’s DOJ has come after me.
Last week, I received a threat on Justice Department letterhead from Aaron Reitz, the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas.
**Today, I’m responding.**
**[Before I tell you more, will you chip in $10 to show you have my back and support my work in the Senate?](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/8046?t=13&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_112726_dojresponsebump&akid=10960%2E5257348%2Eclhlgi)**

Aaron Reitz threatened me with “legal consequences” if I don’t stop investigating and doing oversight of President Trump and the corruption in his administration.
_So why exactly is he threatening me?_
Because I’ve called for oversight and transparency.
Of the massive contributions to Trump’s ballroom, to find out who’s really behind them and whether there’s some kind of crooked bargain at play.
Of Freedom 250, the organization set up to raise money for the Fourth of July celebration.
Of media payments to Donald Trump after he sued ABC and CBS.
Of law firms that have done work for the president after capitulating to his threats.
Essentially, Reitz has made it clear that DOJ will investigate anyone investigating the president.
Here’s the thing, Derek: I’ve read the Constitution.
I know Congress has both the right and the duty to do oversight. And it is crazy to threaten senators for doing their jobs.
**So today, I'm sending a letter to Aaron Reitz telling him that I won’t stop doing my job.**
I’m calling on him to withdraw this absurd request. We’re going to continue doing the oversight that the American people voted for in overwhelming numbers.

body:
The lessons we can learn from this election.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/144155227/662586732/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImViZWEyMTMxLTk2ZWEtZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzE5YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=qmdt8QS_vvx_XTRFz9cC1cE2aAv4R2IOmsPIgSMKH8M=&emci=372b2599-28e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=ebea2131-96ea-f111-91f3-000d3a53319b&ceid=8431045)
---

Peter, before this election is too far in the rearview, I want to take a minute to acknowledge something. Democracy was on the line in this election — and you showed decisively that we’re not willing to let it go to ruin. When President Trump started an unprecedented redistricting crisis, we knew the path ahead would be tough. We acknowledged that democracy is a muscle: to make it strong, we have to exercise it. So we put our heads down and did the work. But even as maps were redrawn everywhere from Texas to Alabama to Florida, it was hard to imagine the historic wins we’d be celebrating today. Because of you, we've taken on fight after fight to defeat Republican gerrymandering, voter suppression, and obstruction. The individual victories are too many to name in one email. On the whole, they were decisive. In this election, the American people spoke in a clear voice that they’re not going to let politicians cheat their way into power. In spite of all those rigged maps, we’ll start next year with Democrats in charge of both chambers of Congress. We’ll see at least 10 state legislative chambers flip from red to blue. We’ll have six new Democratic trifectas. All of this together delivers a powerful statement that we can go up against Donald Trump and his team of anti-democracy radicals — and win. It requires uncompromising resistance and unprecedented mobilization. But we will not cower in the face of threats to representative democracy. Our work is far from over. Republicans are plotting right now to redraw maps before the next cycle — and we could see a state or two start any day now during the lame-duck period. We will fight them (again). We will defeat them (again). Bank on it. Our north star is clearer than ever: Save our democracy today, so we can heal it tomorrow. Peter: You helped make this once-in-a-generation election night possible. Remember how it feels right now. Remember how hard-fought this victory was. Because when we are tested again — and we will be tested again — we’ll need to call on these lessons. We’ll need to summon every ounce of strength and determination to fight. I’m so proud to be part of this movement with you. In solidarity, Eric H. Holder, Jr.

This puts over 58,000 Hoosiers at risk of losing their healthcare coverage in January. Instead of giving working families time to learn a confusing new system and time for the state to ensure compliance and avoid federal penalties, Braun is rushing ahead. Braun Rejects Grace Period for Medicaid Work Requirements Governor Braun’s administration just confirmed that Indiana will not allow the six-month grace period offered by the federal government for Medicaid work requirements. Instead of giving working families time to learn a confusing new system and time for the state to ensure compliance and avoid federal penalties, Braun is rushing ahead.
